_README: Coordinate corrections applied on top of cities.min.json at seed time.
cities.min.json is a trimmed copy of the upstream CSC dataset, so editing
it directly would lose these fixes the next time it is refreshed. Keeping
them here means a refresh picks the corrections back up, and the reason for
each one stays attached to it.
Only add a row where the bundled coordinate is demonstrably not the city.
A tenth of a degree of longitude moves sunrise by ~24 seconds, so this is
worth doing for a city we publish muhurat pages for and not worth doing to
After changing this file, re-seed: `uv run python -m scripts.seed --force`.
Cached day rows for a corrected city are dropped automatically, because
they were computed from the wrong sunrise.

corrections.name: Jaipur
corrections.why: CSC carries a quarter-degree grid point, not the city. The bundled longitude is ~0.21 deg east of Jaipur, which puts sunrise about 50 seconds early.
corrections.source: Wikipedia / GeoNames city point for Jaipur, Rajasthan

corrections.name: Cuttack
corrections.why: Same quarter-degree grid problem, and worse: the bundled longitude is ~0.37 deg east, which puts sunrise about 90 seconds early.
corrections.source: Wikipedia / GeoNames city point for Cuttack, Odisha
